jobs.jobDescription:
About AutoFi

AutoFi is the leading provider of digital commerce technology that powers the sales and finance experiences for the most innovative brands and dealers in automotive. The AutoFi platform enables a more transactional buying experience with $4B in funded loans processed through AutoFi annually. AutoFi’s dynamic selling platform empowers dealers to sell vehicles more efficiently and profitably, both online and in the showroom. We are funded for years of future growth and backed by investors including Crosslink Capital, Santander Holdings USA, SVB Financial Group, Ford, BMW iVentures and JP Morgan Chase.

Our team is diverse - spread out across the U.S. and Canada, we have backgrounds from finance and technology as well as deep experience in all areas of the auto space. We’re empathetic, gritty, curious, and humble owners of this business and are supported by some of the biggest names in the auto and financial industries as commercial partners. We’ve never been more excited about the opportunity in front of us to help transition the auto industry from offline to online. If changing a trillion-dollar industry sounds exciting, we’d love to hear from you.

For more information, visit www.autofi.com.

About the Role
Reporting to the Manager, Partner Support Services, the Dealer Partner Support Specialist is responsible for supporting the ongoing operational health, configuration, and functionality of AutoFi's products and services for our Dealership and Dealer Group partners. Acting as a key point of contact and subject matter expert following implementation, this role responds to partner inquiries, manages program adjustments, troubleshoots issues, and works collaboratively with internal teams and external vendors to ensure programs function as intended and continue to meet evolving business needs.

Partner Support Services plays a key role in operating as the first line of support for all of AutoFi’s clientele. They triage and prioritize all incoming requests, resolve general inquiries, make program settings adjustments, work with vendors to align on integrated functionality, and ensure Clients/Partners are able to connect with the appropriate resources. They monitor expected program functionality, proactively taking steps to resolve potential gaps and capitalize on enhancement opportunities.

An ideal candidate will be a detail-oriented, resourceful problem solver who combines strong customer service skills with technical aptitude and a commitment to accuracy. They will be comfortable managing competing priorities, investigating issues independently, and communicating effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders in a fast paced environment. Success in this role requires accountability, sound judgement, adaptability and a proactive approach to maintaining program health and delivering an exceptional partner experience. This position includes occasional scheduled evening and weekend support coverage to accommodate Dealerships operating hours. Each member of our team is challenged to contribute in a variety of capacities across the entire organization and show their individual strengths, from product to customer experience.

Responsibilities

  • Participate in and contribute to a collaborative, accountable team environment with a culture of open communication through knowledge sharing, constructive feedback, and a willingness to support shared priorities.
  • Develop and maintain proficiency in AutoFi's product suite, integration capabilities, and Dealer Partner use cases, providing informed recommendations to optimize program configurations and functionality.
  • Serve as a primary point of contact for Dealer Partners, responding to inquiries, resolving issues, and managing requests professionally and efficiently in accordance with expected service levels.
  • Maintain and optimize Dealer Partner program settings, configurations, features, and integrations, including working with JSON, XML, CSS, and Regex as needed.
  • Independently validate completed work to ensure configuration changes are accurate, complete, and functioning as intended before considering requests resolved.
  • Perform initial troubleshooting of configuration, integration, and functional issues as needed to identify root causes, resolve common problems, and escalate more complex issues with appropriate supporting details.
  • Collaborate with Account Management, Product, Engineering, and other internal teams, as well as external vendors, to coordinate solutions and support evolving Dealer Partner needs.
  • Proactively monitor Dealer Partner programs to identify functional anomalies, configuration gaps, and opportunities to improve program performance and reliability.
  • Manage a concurrent workload of approximately 20-30 assigned requests through to resolution against expected SLAs, effectively balancing competing priorities, maintaining accurate case documentation, clear stakeholder communication, and timely follow-up through phone, email and text, leveraging specific internal and vendor communications platforms where applicable.
  • Identify recurring issues and opportunities to improve support processes, contributing to the development of standardized procedures, documentation, and best practices, inclusive of the nuances, pros and cons of various approaches.
  • Support first-line inquiries across AutoFi's broader Partner ecosystem as needed through phone, chat and email, leveraging available tools, including AI-assisted solutions, to improve efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Participate in scheduled after-hours support coverage, including a minimum of one Saturday per month.

Qualifications

  • 2-3 years experience working in customer support, technical support, account management or a related customer-facing role, preferably within the SaaS environment.
  • Strong attention to detail, with a demonstrated ability to accurately execute, validate and document work
    Analytical and critical thinking skills, including the ability to independently investigate issues, troubleshoot basic technical problems, and determine when escalation is appropriate.
  • Excellent written/verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly and navigate challenging customer interactions
  • Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritize competing requests and meet established service expectations
  • Technical aptitude and comfort working with software configurations, system settings, integrated applications and AI Agents
  • A proactive, accountable approach to problem-solving, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively across teams
  • Flexibility to participate in scheduled evening and weekend coverage including a minimum of one Saturday per month
  • Familiarity with automotive dealership operations, business models, and personnel responsibilities strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of APIs, JSON, XML, HTML, CSS, and Regex strongly preferred
  • Experience using Salesforce, Jira, Postman, or similar CRM, case management, and API troubleshooting tools preferred.
  • Experience using AI-assisted tools to improve productivity, troubleshooting, or customer support workflows preferred.

Compensation

+ $2,000 performance bonus annually

Additional Information

What's in it for you:

- We offer full training and a competitive total rewards package along with great benefits

- Medical, Dental & Vision coverage - 100% premium coverage for employee / 50+% for dependents

- Flexible work hours

- Remote environment

- Competitive pay

- Visionary leadership team

- Growth opportunities within a dynamic culture

- Wellness & cultural initiatives (fitness challenges, wellness webinars, virtual games, regional activities, etc.)

- Up to $1K per year for employee professional development

- Stock options - we are all owners!

Individual compensation decisions are based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience and qualifications and local market conditions. Please note, the foregoing salary range does not reflect an employee’s total compensation package, which may include bonus, company equity, and health benefits.

AutoFi is an equal opportunity employer. Individuals seeking employment are considered without regards to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or other protected status under all applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances.

Personal Information submitted as part of your application is subject to our website privacy policy, located at https://www.autofi.com/privacy-policy/

jobs.jobDescription:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is building the next generation of industrial robots -- hardware that's powerful, affordable, and designed to scale. We're the largest U.S. industrial robotics company by robots shipped, and our robots are showing up on factory floors everywhere from independent machine shops to NASA and Lockheed Martin. Someone has to make sure those robots actually work -- and someone has to build the team that makes that happen at scale. That's this role.

Note: This role requires up to 25% domestic travel. You're still in the field -- just not living out of a suitcase 2-3 days a week.

Also note: Like every Applications Engineer at Standard Bots, this is not a software engineering role. You are a hands-on industrial automation engineer who also happens to lead people. If you've never commissioned a robotic cell, this isn't the right seat.

The Role

The Applications Engineering Manager is a player-coach. You still know your way around a factory floor -- fixtures, I/O, ladder logic, robot programming, all the things -- and you use that expertise every day, both to stay sharp and to earn the respect of the team you're leading.

You'll manage a team of Applications Engineers across your territory, owning their development, their workload, and the quality of every customer engagement they touch. You'll be the escalation point when installs get complicated, the person who jumps on a plane when a customer situation needs senior eyes, and the one who sets the standard for what great applications engineering looks like at Standard Bots.

This is still a hands-on role. You're not managing from a desk. You're leading from the front.

You'll report directly to the VP of Applications Engineering.

What You'll Do

Team Leadership & Development

- Manage and develop a team of Applications Engineers across your territory -- setting expectations, coaching on technical and customer-facing skills, and building a team that executes at a high level

- Own capacity planning and workload distribution across your team -- making sure the right engineer is on the right job and nobody is drowning

- Be the technical and cultural standard-setter for your team; the bar you hold yourself to is the bar your team rises to

- Conduct regular 1:1s, performance conversations, and development planning -- you invest in your people's growth, not just their output

Territory & Customer Ownership

- Own the applications engineering function for your territory -- from pre-sales POC support through post-install customer success

- Serve as the senior technical escalation point for complex integrations, difficult customer situations, or installs that aren't going as planned

- Partner closely with your Regional Sales Manager on territory priorities, pipeline, and customer strategy -- you're the technical counterpart to their commercial leadership

- Maintain strong relationships with key customer accounts in your territory; they should know you by name and trust your judgment

Hands-On Technical Work

- Stay sharp and stay in it -- you're still designing solutions, reviewing integrations, commissioning cells, and supporting installs when the situation calls for it

- Lead or co-lead technically complex or strategically important customer engagements yourself

- Review and sign off on solution designs, POCs, and integration plans produced by your team

- Travel to customer sites as needed -- up to 25% domestically -- for escalations, key installs, and customer relationship moments

Standards & Continuous Improvement

- Define and enforce the standard for how applications engineering work gets done in your territory -- documentation, handoffs, commissioning checklists, customer training quality

- Feed territory-level learnings back to the broader applications engineering organization and to product and engineering teams

- Help build the playbooks, templates, and training materials that make every AE on your team better and every deployment more repeatable

What We're Looking For

- The same trifecta as our Applications Engineers -- you're genuinely fluent across mechanical, electrical, and software: PLC programming and ladder logic, pneumatics, DC power systems, robot programming, Python scripting, CAD

- 5+ years of hands-on applications engineering, systems integration, or automation engineering experience -- you've done the field work and done it well

- 2+ years of people management or team lead experience -- you've led engineers, given hard feedback, and helped someone grow

- Strong customer-facing presence -- you can manage a difficult customer conversation, set expectations clearly, and represent Standard Bots credibly at a senior level

- Experience managing a distributed team or territory; you know how to lead people you don't see every day

- Comfort with up to 25% domestic travel for escalations, key customer engagements, and team support

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, or a related engineering discipline -- or equivalent hands-on experience that tells the same story

Nice to Have

- Prior experience with collaborative robots (UR, Fanuc, KUKA, ABB, or similar)

- Background scaling an applications engineering or field engineering function -- you've helped build something, not just inherited it

- Experience with vision systems, force/torque sensing, or custom end-of-arm tooling

- Familiarity with machine tending, palletizing, welding, or assembly automation applications

Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $140,000 to $180,000, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

jobs.jobDescription:
About Jade Biosciences

Jade Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing best-in-class therapies that address critical unmet needs in autoimmune diseases. Jade’s lead candidate, JADE101, targets the cytokine APRIL, and is currently being evaluated for the treatment of immunoglobulin A nephropathy. Jade’s pipeline also includes JADE201, an afucosylated anti-BAFF-R monoclonal antibody, as well as JADE301, an anti-IFN-β monoclonal antibody. Jade was launched based on assets licensed from Paragon Therapeutics, an antibody discovery engine founded by Fairmount. For more information, visit JadeBiosciences.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn.

Role Overview

We are seeking an experienced and mission-driven Medical Director in Clinical Development to lead and support clinical programs in nephrology, with a focus on rare or immune-mediated kidney diseases. This role is ideal for a physician-scientist who thrives in a small biotech environment where agility, cross-functional collaboration, and scientific leadership are essential. The Medical Director will play a key role in advancing Jade’s pipeline through clinical development. This newly created position will report to the Executive Medical Director of Clinical Development. This is a fully remote role and will require some travel.

Key Responsibilities

Clinical Development

  • Lead the design, execution, and oversight of clinical trials in nephrology, including protocol development, study monitoring, and data interpretation.
  • Serve as Medical Monitor for ongoing trials, ensuring patient safety and scientific integrity.
  • Collaborate with clinical operations, regulatory, and biometrics teams to ensure trial success and compliance.
  • Educate and advise clinical sites/investigators to support enrollment and optimal study conduct, including presenting at investigator meetings and/or site initiation visits, and serving as the medical point of contact for site staff questions about patient eligibility, and providing input into patient safety assessment and management
  • Provide medical expertise and support to external partners, vendors, and contractors as required to ensure smooth program execution
  • Communicate effectively, orally and in writing, with internal and external stakeholders regarding the assigned clinical program, including the CMO, CEO, external medical experts and others.

Regulatory and Scientific Contributions

  • Contribute to the preparation of regulatory documents (INDs, NDAs, briefing documents, etc.).
  • Support interactions with regulatory authorities and ethics committees.
  • Stay current with scientific literature and competitive landscape in nephrology and related fields.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with translational science, biomarker, and commercial teams to align clinical strategy with broader company goals.
  • Provide medical input into lifecycle planning and early market preparation.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Begin building relationships with key opinion leaders (KOLs), investigators, and advocacy groups in nephrology.
  • Represent the company at scientific meetings, advisory boards, and industry events.

Qualifications

  • MD (or equivalent medical degree); board certification in nephrology strongly preferred.
  • 3+ years of experience as a nephrologist in academia or industry, and/or experience in nephrology clinical trials or rare disease programs.
  • Experience in clinical trial design, execution, and medical monitoring.
  • Strong clinical judgment, scientific rigor, and regulatory knowledge.
  • Ability to work independently and thrive in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to influence and motivate cross-functional teams, manage a diverse set of stakeholders, and work closely with team leaders
  • High ethical standards and impeccable integrity
  • Exercise sound judgment in managing complex, confidential, and regulated information.

Position Location

This is a remote role; periodic travel to team and company events is required.

The anticipated salary range for candidates for this role is $270,000 - $300,000. The final salary offered will depend on several factors, which may include, but not limited to, relevant years of experience, educational background, and geography.

As part of the I-9 verification of authorization to work in the United States, Jade Bioscience participates in E-Verify. To learn more about E-Verify please review this poster.

Jade Biosciences is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.jobDescription:
About Latent

Latent is the enterprise pharmacy intelligence platform, powered by a clinical agentic engine, that enables health systems to grow their pharmacy operations and serve more patients. One engine works across the pharmacy journey to identify patients who qualify for care, improve medication access, capture eligible prescriptions and support patients throughout treatment. Latent’s platform enables more than 60 leading health systems that collectively serve an estimated 70 million people. Founded by Sriram “Sri” Somasundaram and Rishabh Jain, Latent has raised $80 million from Transformation Capital, Spark Capital, Conviction, General Catalyst, Y Combinator, and others.

The Role

We’re building the intelligence layer of American healthcare. Our systems sit directly in critical workflows and power how clinical AI is delivered and used in practice. You’ll be working on securing all aspects of Latent’s code, cloud, AI, and IT systems. You will be partnering with all Latent employees across engineering, product, legal, and GTM to safely enable Latent employees to move quickly without sacrificing security and compliance.

What You'll Do

You’ll be a Security generalist, helping define, lead, and execute the roadmap in all aspects of Security. Here are some of the areas you will work in:

  • Cloud Security
    Mature and harden Latent’s cloud environment from a security and compliance standpoint into a secure-by-default stance so developers can ship code with confidence and the Infrastructure team doesn’t have to worry that their next Terraform apply will put everything on the open internet.

  • AI Security
    Employees at Latent use a lot of AI. Help us give all of our employees access to the latest and greatest AI-powered tools in a secure and compliant way so our agents don’t run amok and do the wrong thing.

  • Data Security
    Latent’s business thrives on giving our users deep insights into their patient data, their pharmacy performance, and how our AI is performing. Help us secure our data warehouse so that our internal employees and customers get the insight they need without sacrificing our commitment to patient security and privacy.

  • Application and Product Security
    Latent’s developers ship a lot of code. Help us come up with ways to automate all aspects of the SDLC from a security perspective to ensure security is built in instead of being a bolt-on afterwards. In addition, as Latent plans the next iteration of its application and agentic platform, help us come up with the right security requirements for new product features and enhancements.

  • IT Security
    Help our hard-working IT folks secure Latent employee devices and applications. Automate security around IT and business applications including user lifecycle provisioning, just-in-time access, elevated access provisioning, and device hardening to ensure employees can do their job securely without thinking about security.

  • Incident Detection and Response
    Help the Security team investigate potential incidents, build detections that are specific to Latent’s environment, and work with our AI-native MDR service to improve accuracy around escalated incidents.

What We're Looking For

You’re a builder who holds yourself and others to high standards. You can design, develop, and create security automations and workflows using AI that can scale Latent’s security team.

  • Ownership: You don’t hand off problems or wait for someone to tell you what to do. Find our gaps, risks, and vulnerabilities and implement the solution.

  • Bias for Action: You won’t wait for someone else to solve a problem you’re in a position to solve.

  • A Yes Mindset: Latent’s Security team is not a no factory. While we put our foot down when the risk is high, our goal is to find creative solutions that 1) Understand what an employee actually needs and 2) That balances speed and security.

  • Automation Mindset: You’re always looking for ways to move faster by automating repetitive or manual work.

  • Complexity Management: You’re good at planning and building the simplest solution that gets the job done, with an eye towards the future as Latent scales quickly. You can take a complex and large product and break it down into focused, iterative steps that incrementally make our security and compliance posture better.

  • Product Focus: You’re comfortable working closely with the customers that use Latent’s security program: Latent’s employees! You love sitting alongside folks from all areas of the company, understanding their day to day, and crafting the perfect solution for them both now and in the future.

Technical Qualifications

We really are looking for a little bit of a unicorn and someone who has done it all when it comes to security. If you’ve worked in multiple of these areas, this is the place for you!

  • You aren’t afraid to use coding agents to contribute solutions directly to the code base! (You don’t have to be a coding wizard Harry, but you do need to understand basic engineering principles to give your coding agent positive feedback if it spits out the wrong solution)

  • You’ve built out IAM workflows (Okta, SSO, SAML, JIT provisioning) to give employees just the right amount of access to get their job done

  • You’ve designed and rolled out managed settings for AI tools and coding agents to make sure employees have a good sandbox to work in to get their jobs done with AI

  • You have collaborated with developers to help them write secure code and secure features.

  • You’ve helped harden AWS cloud and CI/CD environments (Think well-scoped IAM roles, hardening cloud environments to CIS standards, picking the right CSPM and driving down a findings backlog ect..)

  • You’ve helped build and maintain a vulnerability management program all the way up the stack (Server/Container/3rd Party OSS/Custom Code)

  • You’ve automated security and compliance requirements for MacOS and BYOD endpoints using an MDM

jobs.jobDescription:
About Jade Biosciences

Jade Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing best-in-class therapies that address critical unmet needs in autoimmune diseases. Jade’s lead candidate, JADE101, targets the cytokine APRIL, and is currently being evaluated for the treatment of immunoglobulin A nephropathy. Jade’s pipeline also includes JADE201, an afucosylated anti-BAFF-R monoclonal antibody, as well as JADE301, an anti-IFN-β monoclonal antibody. Jade was launched based on assets licensed from Paragon Therapeutics, an antibody discovery engine founded by Fairmount. For more information, visit JadeBiosciences.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn.

Role Overview

Jade is developing potentially transformational, disease-modifying therapies for people living with autoimmune diseases. With three biologics programs in the clinic and multiple ongoing studies from Phase I to Phase III, we are seeking an experienced Executive Director, Clinical Supply Management to join our CMC leadership team and make sure every patient in our trials receives the right investigational product, on time.

Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer (Head of CMC), you will own clinical supply strategy, planning and execution for all Jade programs. You will shape and scale the Clinical Supply Management function, growing and mentoring a team of internal employees and contractors, and you will lead a global network of CMOs and logistics partners supporting complex, multi-country and multi-site studies with ambitious timelines and enrollment targets.

This is a high-impact role for a self-starter who combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You will work closely with Clinical Operations and Clinical Development to secure supply for every planned study, help prepare the supply chain for BLA filing, launch and commercial readiness, and contribute directly to Jade’s key corporate goals.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and build the function: Provide strategic and operational leadership for Jade’s Clinical Supply Management function. Further develop and scale the team through a combination of internal headcount and external partners, including recruiting, onboarding and mentoring team members and consultants. Develop robust business processes and SOP in close collaboration with the Quality function.
  • Define the clinical supply strategy: Develop and implement the clinical supply strategy for all Jade programs, from early-stage (Phase 1/2) through late-stage (Phase 3) development, with a forward-looking view toward BLA filing, product launch and commercial readiness.
  • Plan demand and supply: Build and maintain integrated global demand forecasts and supply plans based on protocols, enrollment projections and site activation plans. Balance drug product availability, shelf life, overage and cost, and update plans as studies evolve. Advise on potential risk and challenges to Senior Management and peer groups such as Clinical Operations and Development.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally: Partner closely with Clinical Operations and Clinical Development on study-specific supply strategies, and with Quality, Regulatory Affairs and CMC to forecast, align and continuously update supply requirements for ongoing and future studies. Develop options and recommendations for stakeholders and senior management.
  • Select and manage CMOs and suppliers: Select, contract and manage clinical supply CMOs, depots, couriers, logistics providers, and other critical suppliers. Set clear performance expectations and KPIs, and build strong partnerships that ensure quality, reliability and cost-effective supply.
  • Oversee clinical supply operations: Direct labeling, packaging, blinding, cold-chain storage and global distribution for all drug product formats, including vials, pre-filled syringes and autoinjectors. Manage comparator sourcing, expiry extensions, relabeling, returns, reconciliation and destruction.
  • Manage IRT and inventory: Define supply requirements for IRT/IxRS systems, including resupply strategies and user acceptance testing, and monitor inventory at depots and sites to prevent stock-outs and minimize waste.
  • Ensure compliance and quality: Maintain full compliance with Jade SOPs, cGMP, GDP, GCP, ICH guidelines and applicable global regulatory and import/export requirements. Partner with Quality on batch release (including QP release for EU studies), deviations and change controls, keep the function inspection-ready, and contribute to regulatory submissions (IND, IMPD, CTA).
  • Own the budget and reporting: Manage the clinical supply budget, and report regularly and concisely to stakeholders and senior management on inventory, supply and demand, changes and risks across all programs.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Life Sciences, Chemical Engineering or a related field.
  • 15+ years of progressive experience in clinical supply chain management, ideally with biologics, including significant experience leading teams. Experience in commercial supply chain management is a plus.
  • Proven experience managing clinical supply for biologics in vials within cold-chain environments, using local and multinational CMOs; experience with pre-filled syringes and combination products such as autoinjectors highly preferred.
  • Experience supporting multiple early- and late-stage programs, including multi-country Phase 3 studies and bridging studies for biologic combination products.
  • Comprehensive understanding of global regulatory and import/export requirements across Europe, North America, China, Japan and Rest of World (ROW), and strong working knowledge of cGMP, GDP and GCP.
  • Hands-on experience with IRT/IxRS systems, clinical supply forecasting tools and budget management.
  • Demonstrated success building and scaling clinical supply functions, including hiring, onboarding and managing team members and consultants to meet critical milestones.
  • Exceptional communication, leadership and interpersonal skills, with a track record of aligning CMC, Quality, Regulatory Affairs and Clinical teams and building trusting relationships with external CMO partners.
  • A strategic thinker with a proven execution record, strong problem-solving skills and the ability to thrive in a complex, fast-paced clinical development environment.

Position Location

This is a remote role; periodic travel to team and company events is required.

The anticipated salary range for candidates for this role is $280,000 - $300,000. The final salary offered will depend on several factors, which may include, but not limited to, relevant years of experience, educational background, and geography.

As part of the I-9 verification of authorization to work in the United States, Jade Bioscience participates in E-Verify. To learn more about E-Verify please review this poster.

Jade Biosciences is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.jobDescription:
About Latent

Latent is the enterprise pharmacy intelligence platform, powered by a clinical agentic engine, that enables health systems to grow their pharmacy operations and serve more patients. One engine works across the pharmacy journey to identify patients who qualify for care, improve medication access, capture eligible prescriptions and support patients throughout treatment.

Latent’s platform enables more than 60+ leading health systems that collectively serve an estimated 70 million people. Founded by Sri Somasundaram and Rishabh Jain, Latent has raised $80 million from Transformation Capital, Spark Capital, Conviction, General Catalyst, Y Combinator, and others.

The Role

As Clinical GTM Lead, you will be Latent’s pharmacy subject matter expert for prospective and current customers. You’ll work with Sales on demos, clinical diligence, and executive conversations; support Partner Experience through implementations and account growth; and bring what you hear from customers back to Product. You’ll help pharmacy leaders understand how Latent fits their workflows, where it can make a difference, and how we approach clinical quality and patient safety.

Your presence should give customers confidence that experienced pharmacists help build Latent and support its products. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working directly with customers and turning clinical insight into practical action.

What You’ll Do

Clinical sales partnership

  • Lead the clinical portions of sales calls, product demos, diligence, and executive meetings. Address questions about pharmacy operations, medication access, and how Latent fits into existing workflows.

  • Partner with Sales to anticipate objections, explain the product clearly to clinical and nonclinical stakeholders, and build trust through accurate, direct answers.

Customer implementation and growth

  • Work with Partner Experience to understand each customer’s workflows, support implementation decisions, and help pharmacy teams adopt the product successfully.

  • Join strategic account conversations to identify opportunities for deeper use, retention, and expansion that serve customer and patient needs.

Product insight and clinical accuracy

  • Turn customer feedback and clinical requirements into clear recommendations for Product, balancing clinical value, operational feasibility, and business impact.

  • Review customer-facing claims, presentations, and guidance for clinical accuracy and sound judgment around patient safety, compliance, and product positioning.

Tools that help the team scale

  • Create reusable clinical presentations, diligence responses, workflow guidance, and answers to common customer questions.

  • Equip Sales and Partner Experience to handle recurring clinical questions confidently while knowing when to bring in deeper pharmacy expertise.

What Success Looks Like

  • Within six months: You are a trusted clinical partner on our most important sales opportunities and customer accounts, and you have built materials and processes that Sales and Partner Experience use regularly.

  • Within 12 months: Your work has strengthened clinical confidence throughout the sales process, supported retention and expansion, and established a clear feedback loop among customers, Latent’s clinical team, and Product.

What We’re Looking For

  • A PharmD from an accredited institution and an active or recently active pharmacist license in at least one U.S. state.

  • At least seven years of relevant experience across pharmacy practice, clinical operations, healthcare technology, or related work, including meaningful experience with pharmacy workflows.

  • Strong understanding of medication access and the day-to-day needs of pharmacists, pharmacy leaders, and the organizations they serve.

  • Experience working directly with customers and communicating with clinical, operational, and executive stakeholders. You can lead a detailed workflow discussion and an executive conversation with equal confidence.

  • A record of owning clinical, operational, product, or customer outcomes, with the ability to turn clinical requirements into practical solutions.

  • Clear writing and presentation skills. You make complex clinical topics understandable and create materials that other teams can use.

  • Sound judgment about clinical risk, patient safety, compliance, and the claims we make about our product.

  • Comfort learning and explaining technical and AI products, and working closely with commercial and technical teams.

  • A hands-on, low-ego approach. You take ownership, move through ambiguity, and help the team get the work done.

Nice to Have

  • Experience at a healthcare technology, digital health, or pharmacy technology company.

  • Experience supporting enterprise healthcare sales, strategic accounts, or technology implementations in a pharmacy organization.

  • Familiarity with AI products or clinical decision support tools.

  • Relationships with pharmacy executives or health system pharmacy leaders, or experience speaking at industry events.

Why Join Latent

  • Help more patients get the medications they need by improving how pharmacy teams work.

  • Work closely with Sales, Partner Experience, Product, and our clinical team on problems that matter to customers.

  • Shape how Latent earns clinical trust as the company grows, with the ownership to build what the team needs.

jobs.jobDescription:
You: The champion who turns belief in liberty into the resources to defend it. Every case PLF wins starts with someone who chose to fund the fight. You'll be that person's trusted partner. You'll get to know what drives our donors, show them the real impact of their giving, and invite them to make bold investments in freedom.

Them: Bureaucrats, city councils, mayors, governors, and federal agencies stripping Americans of their rights every day. There’s a lot of government overreach out there, and it’s backed by seemingly endless resources. But fortunately, like all lumbering giants, abusive government is most vulnerable when countered by individuals who act strategically and nimbly, take calculated risks, have each other’s backs, and are confident in and passionate for the cause—the very sort of swashbucklers we employ in spades here at PLF.

Us: We fight back. Pacific Legal Foundation is the nation’s first and most successful public interest law firm dedicated to vindicating individual liberty. PLF has an unmatched record in the United States Supreme Court, with 18 victories out of 21 litigated at the Court—including three victories last term. We also have nearly two hundred active cases across the nation.

We are a next-generation public interest law firm. That means we aren’t interested in doing the same thing as everyone else. We aspire to be the best player in a constantly changing game.

Here’s what you get to do in this role:

The Senior Donor Relations Officer is responsible for developing and managing a portfolio of high-capacity current and prospective major gift donors, with responsibility for the identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of significant philanthropic relationships supporting Pacific Legal Foundation’s mission and strategic priorities.

The Senior Donor Relations Officer will develop and execute sophisticated donor strategies, build meaningful long-term relationships with donors and prospects, and secure significant new, renewed, and increased philanthropic commitments.

The successful candidate will be an accomplished frontline fundraiser with exceptional relationship-building and communication skills, strong fundraising judgment, and a demonstrated record of closing significant major gifts. The position requires a highly organized, persistent, disciplined, and self-directed professional who can operate with substantial independence while collaborating effectively with PLF leadership, attorneys, and Development colleagues.

Getting down to brass tacks, your specific job duties likely will include:

  • Managing a portfolio of approximately 100 high-capacity major gift donors and prospects and achieve established fundraising, engagement, and solicitation goals.
  • Developing and executing individualized strategies for donor qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Personally soliciting and securing significant new, renewed, and increased gifts, including six-figure and seven-figure commitments.
  • Building trusted, long-term donor relationships by understanding donors’ interests, motivations, and philanthropic priorities and serving as their primary PLF relationship manager.
  • Creating meaningful donor engagement and stewardship opportunities that demonstrate the impact of philanthropy and connect donors to PLF’s litigation, policy, and strategic priorities.
  • Strategically engaging PLF executives, attorneys, trustees, and other organizational leaders in donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
  • Identifying and advancing new major gift prospects and recognize opportunities for multi-year, planned, blended, campaign, and other complex gifts in collaboration with Development colleagues.
  • Maintaining a disciplined portfolio and moves management, including donor strategies, next steps, solicitation plans, revenue projections, contact reports, and accurate CRM records.
  • Contributing to Development team strategy and serve as a resource to colleagues on complex donor relationships and major gift opportunities.

The ideal candidate will have:

  • 8+ years of professional fundraising experience, including substantial frontline major gift experience.
  • A demonstrated record of personally cultivating, soliciting, and closing significant major gifts, preferably including six and seven figure commitments.
  • Exceptional interpersonal, listening, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to build trusted relationships and communicate complex ideas clearly and compellingly.
  • Strong strategic judgment, initiative, organization, and personal accountability, with the ability to operate independently in a results-oriented environment.
  • Proficiency with fundraising CRM systems and disciplined portfolio and moves management practices.
  • A willingness to travel up to 50% throughout the United States, with a heavy focus throughout California, to meet with donors and prospects.
  • A sincere appreciation for PLF’s mission

Preferred experience. Previous experience with a pro-liberty organization, legal advocacy organization, public policy organization, or similar mission-driven institution is a plus. Experience with Salesforce or a comparable fundraising CRM is also preferred.

General information:

Pacific Legal Foundation identifies and litigates important legal issues to set landmark precedents that will benefit Americans nationwide. Using strategic and principled litigation, communications, and research, we battle for freedom in the nation’s courts and the court of public opinion.

As a national nonprofit organization, PLF has brick-and-mortar offices in Sacramento, California and Arlington, Virginia, although approximately half of the staff work from home offices across the country. You may work from any of our offices or request to work remotely, although strong preference will be given to California-based candidates.

Salary range and benefits:

This is a full-time, permanent position. PLF is committed to recruiting and retaining the highest-quality talent available nationwide, and we offer a total compensation package that includes a competitive salary, medical and dental insurance, and employer-paid retirement savings. We take work-life balance seriously through our generous paid leave and flextime policies. To learn more about the starting salary range and benefits options, please apply.

How to apply:

Qualified candidates should submit the following application materials:

  • Résumé
  • Cover letter detailing the candidate’s sincere interest in Pacific Legal Foundation, its mission, and the Senior Donor Relations Officer position

About Jade Biosciences

Jade Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing best-in-class therapies that address critical unmet needs in autoimmune diseases. Jade’s lead candidate, JADE101, targets the cytokine APRIL, and is currently being evaluated for the treatment of immunoglobulin A nephropathy. Role Overview

As the Associate Director of Development Outsourcing, you will play a key role in supporting the sourcing and strategic management of Jade's external vendors. This role will partner closely with Development Operations and study teams to support vendor sourcing, contracting, governance, and the development of strong vendor relationships across clinical development programs from Phase I through Phase IV.

The successful candidate will work cross-functionally to drive effective execution, support issue resolution, and contribute to continuous improvement of Development Outsourcing processes. This newly created role will report to the Director, Development outsourcing. This is a fully remote role and will require occasional travel.

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary Development Outsourcing lead for assigned studies and programs, partnering closely with cross-functional study teams and external vendors to ensure successful execution of outsourcing activities.
  • Implement outsourcing strategies and plans established by Development Outsourcing leadership while independently managing day-to-day vendor-related activities for assigned studies.
  • Provide outsourcing expertise and recommendations to study teams regarding vendor selection, contract strategy, oversight, and issue resolution.
  • Ensure outsourcing deliverables, timelines, and decisions are executed efficiently and aligned with study objectives.
  • Lead vendor sourcing and evaluation activities in support of Development Programs, including preparation of RFI/RFP materials, proposal review, bid defense coordination, comparative analyses, and recommendation development.
  • Lead the development, negotiation, and execution of vendor agreements, including Confidentiality Agreements, Master Service Agreements, Statements of Work, Change Orders, rate cards, Letters of Intent, and other vendor-related agreements.

  • Support vendor governance activities by preparing materials, tracking actions, monitoring performance metrics, and ensuring commitments are executed.
  • Monitor vendor performance and support implementation of corrective and preventive actions when needed.
  • Partner closely with Development Operations, Clinical Quality Assurance, Legal, Finance, and other stakeholders to ensure effective vendor oversight and execution.
  • Support vendor qualification, audit readiness, inspection preparedness, and oversight activities in collaboration with Clinical Quality Assurance.
  • Maintain documentation related to vendor selection, contracting, governance, performance management, and issue resolution.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of Development Outsourcing processes, tools, templates, and best practices.
  • Operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment by balancing urgent issues, strategic priorities, and routine responsibilities across multiple concurrent activities.

  • Demonstrate initiative and accountability by driving decisions, resolving obstacles, and ensuring commitments are completed.

  • Proven ability to independently manage complex outsourcing activities across multiple studies and stakeholders.

  • Ability to identify risks, make timely decisions, and drive resolution of issues with limited direction.
  • Strong communication, negotiation, influence, and relationship management skills.

jobs.jobDescription:
Actian is the company behind the Data Intelligence Platform — an enterprise solution that helps organisations discover, govern, and trust their data at scale. Our platform connects metadata, data lineage, data quality, and business context into a single knowledge graph, enabling enterprises to turn raw data into reliable decisions. We operate globally, move fast, and build for the long term.

Software engineering is being redefined. The engineers who will shape the next decade of product development are not the ones who write the most code — they are the ones who know how to think clearly, ship confidently, and use every tool available to them, including AI, to multiply their impact.

The Actian Data Intelligence Platform helps teams find, understand, and use AI-ready data under clear governance. It connects metadata, data lineage, data quality, and business context into a single knowledge graph, so enterprises can turn raw data into reliable decisions — the trusted foundation that AI agents increasingly depend on to work. We operate globally, move fast, and build for the long term.

The Data Intelligence Platform has to deploy, operate, and pass audits in every one of the environments our customers run — public cloud, private cloud, and on-premises. We are standing up a dedicated platform team to make that possible, and we are hiring the leader who will build it.

This is a hands-on director role. You will stand up and lead a newly formed platform team, hire and grow it, and build alongside it from day one: you will design the platform services, write infrastructure code, and set the engineering standards the rest of engineering relies on.

We are an AI-first engineering organization, and in this role AI is how the work gets done. AI agents run operational tasks, AI accelerates the team's own engineering, and AI replaces tools we pay for today but no longer need. You will also build the infrastructure that runs the AI and ML workloads inside our product.

What You Will Own:

  • Platform services for the Data Intelligence Platform, including the infrastructure behind the data catalog, the knowledge graph, and the APIs that power customer integrations.

  • Cloud-agnostic deployment of the Platform across AWS, a second public cloud (Azure or Google Cloud), and customer on-premises and private-cloud environments — including packaging, installation, upgrades, and supportability.

  • The internal developer platform and CI/CD, including GitOps delivery, so engineering teams ship safely and quickly.

  • Security operations and compliance evidence for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and GDPR — including EU data residency — in partnership with the security team.

  • Cloud cost management and FinOps, with clear cost visibility and accountability across every environment.

  • Infrastructure for the AI and ML workloads used by the Platform.

  • Observability, reliability, and incident response for the services the team runs, including the team's on-call rotation.

  • Building and growing the team — hiring platform engineers, setting the operating model, and establishing the standards and rituals the team works by.

What You Will Deliver in Your First 12 Months:

  • High-functioning platform team: an operating model in place, and clear ownership boundaries with the product engineering teams you serve.

  • Portable, cloud-agnostic deployments: one deployment model that runs the Platform on AWS, on at least one other cloud, and on customer infrastructure — defined as code and delivered through GitOps.

  • AI agents running operations: agents that handle routine operational work — triage, remediation, change validation, and reporting — with measurable reductions in manual effort and a smaller tool footprint.

  • Platform foundations for the data catalog, the knowledge graph, and integration APIs: scalable, observable infrastructure that product teams build on.

  • Compliance automation and audit readiness: evidence for SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and GDPR collected automatically from the platform rather than assembled by hand before each audit.

We expect this leader to treat AI as part of the platform. That means you will:

  • Design and run AI agents that operate infrastructure under clear guardrails — human approval for high-risk changes, and full audit trails.

  • Review our current tooling and retire tools that AI agents or simpler automation can replace, with a cost and risk case for each change.

  • Use AI coding and operations assistants in your own daily work, and set the standard for how the team uses them.

  • Build the compute, data, and access patterns that let AI and ML workloads run reliably in every environment we support.

What You Bring:

  • 10+ years in platform engineering, infrastructure, DevOps, or SRE, including 3+ years managing engineers — with experience building or scaling a team, not only running an established one.

  • AI-first mindset, making extensive use of this technology for accelerating developments.

  • A track record of shipping on-premises or self-hosted software that customers install and run in their own environments.

  • Deep, hands-on experience with Kubernetes in production, infrastructure as code (Terraform/Terragrunt), and GitOps delivery with Argo CD or similar tooling.

  • Strong AWS experience, and the judgment to design for portability rather than lock-in to a single cloud.

  • Hands-on experience operating systems under SOC 2, ISO 27001, and GDPR controls, including data-residency requirements.

  • Experience managing cloud costs and making cost trade-offs explicit to engineering and business leaders.

  • Clear written communication, suited to a fully remote team across US and EU time zones.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience running infrastructure for data platforms, data catalogs, or graph databases.

  • Production experience on Azure or Google Cloud in addition to AWS.

  • Experience with air-gapped or restricted-network customer deployments.

  • Experience building infrastructure for AI and ML workloads, including model serving and vector or graph data stores.

  • Observability with OpenTelemetry or comparable tooling, from instrumentation through alerting.

  • Privileged access management with StrongDM or a comparable tool.

What We Value:

We value autonomy over process, outcomes over activity, and builders over theorists. This role suits someone who thrives when handed a hard problem, a team to build, and the space to figure it out — and who uses every tool available, including AI, to multiply the team's impact.

How You Will Work:

You will report to the SVP of Engineering and work closely with product engineering, security, customer success, and support. The role is fully remote from the US, UK, Spain, France or Germany, with at least four hours a day of overlap with both US Eastern Time and Central European Time. Expect occasional travel for team offsites and company-wide meetings.

What We Offer:

  • The chance to be part of an innovative, fast-growing company making a significant impact in the data management space.
  • Collaboration with a passionate and diverse team.
  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
  • Flexible work arrangements (remote or hybrid).
  • Opportunities for professional growth and development.

Compensation

Additional Information

Why Join Us? At Actian, we are passionate about innovation and teamwork. This role is perfect for someone who thrives in a dynamic environment, loves creating an efficient and welcoming workspace, and enjoys working closely with a talented team.

Interested? We’d love to hear from you! Let’s discuss how you can contribute to our success while growing your career with us.

We value diversity at our company. jobs.jobDescription:
Our Mission:

6sense's mission is to multiply what matters: growth, retention, and efficiency. We envision a future where companies, teams and people reach their full potential.

Our People:

People are the heart and soul of 6sense. We serve with passion and purpose. We live by our Being 6sense values of Win as One Team, Stay Curious, Do The Right Thing, Own the Outcome, and Create Belonging. Every 6sensor plays a part in deﬁning the future of our industry-leading technology. 6sense is a place where difference-makers roll up their sleeves, take risks, act with integrity, and measure success by the value we create for our customers. We want 6sense to be the best chapter of your career.

Product Lead, Predictive Platform

Are you a strategic thinker with a deep background in predictive modeling and a passion for leading teams? At 6sense, our differentiation is built on our ability to accurately predict intent and buyer behavior. We are looking for a Product Lead to own our Predictive Platform—the foundational engine that powers our entire intelligence layer and defines how the world's leading B2B brands identify their next customers.

This is a Player/Coach role. You will be the primary driver of our core predictive foundation and cross-model initiatives while simultaneously serving as the people manager and program leader for a specialized pod of Product Managers. You will oversee the roadmap for how we train, measure, and scale the models that power everything from Fit and Intent to Engagement and Triage.

Why 6sense?

  • AI That Builds Pipe, Not Hype: Our Revenue AI™ identifies accounts ready to buy, crafts the right message, and qualifies meetings automatically. We don’t just surface data—we deliver intelligence and action.
  • Crack the Dark Funnel™: Less than 3% of buyers engage early. We uncover hidden buying signals, decode the “breadcrumb trails,” and help revenue teams connect with buyers in ways they never could before.
  • Orchestrate the Full Journey: From dynamic audience creation to multi-channel engagement, we empower marketers to reach the right accounts, at the right time, with the right message—across advertising, email, web, and sales.
  • Arm Operations Teams: Integrate insights, centralize audience creation, and maximize impact by connecting 6sense with your tech stack. We’re the single canvas for your entire GTM strategy.

Your Impact

As Product Lead, Predictive Platform, you will:

  • Lead and Scale a Specialized Pod. Act as a formal people manager for a pod of Product Managers focused on specialized modeling and intelligence initiatives. You will be responsible for their growth, performance, and alignment with the broader intelligence strategy.
  • Own the Core Predictive Foundation. Personally drive the strategy for our core models. You will define the roadmap for how these models are consumed by downstream applications across the entire 6sense ecosystem.
  • Drive Cross-Model Initiatives. Establish the global standards and methodologies for ongoing model training, feedback loops, and accuracy measurement to ensure our predictions remain the industry benchmark.
  • Maximize Model Leverage. Enforce a "build once, use everywhere" philosophy, ensuring that platform engines provide maximum value to all surface apps and specialized use cases.
  • Be a Strategic Partner to Leadership. Partner directly with the Head of Intelligence Product to align the predictive roadmap with company strategy, surfacing model risks early and identifying opportunities for portfolio tradeoffs.

Strategic Themes You'll Drive

  • Customer Trust and Reliability. Drive the strategy for building high-integrity intelligence that is trusted by enterprise leaders and adapts to a wide range of global business requirements.
  • Leveraged Engine Strategy. Move toward an operating model where core predictive engines are seamlessly consumed by all App teams, reducing duplication and accelerating time-to-market.
  • Data-to-Model Integrity. Ensure the connective tissue between our data foundation and our predictive layer is robust and high performing.

What You'll Bring

  • People Leadership. Proven experience building and leading product teams. You know how to coach PMs through complex roadmaps and create a culture of high accountability.
  • Predictive Product Mastery. Deep expertise in predictive modeling, machine learning lifecycles, and data science collaboration from a product perspective. You have a track record of shipping complex ML-driven products at scale.
  • Operating Rigor. You build operating rhythms that turn messy data and model dependencies into clean execution. You focus on the methodologies that ensure long-term product performance.
  • B2B Mindset. Strong understanding of B2B data models and how predictive scoring drives GTM outcomes.
  • Experience. 8-10+ years in Product Management, with a focus on AI, ML, or Data Science products, including 3-5+ years of formal people management experience.

Why You’ll Love This Role

  • Impact: Your work creates the Predictive Core for the entire company, ensuring our foundational modeling engines remain the most accurate and trusted in the B2B market.
  • Innovation: You will define the Predictive Lifecycle Strategy, building the architectural leverage that allows our modeling teams to move from discovery to platform-wide deployment with high velocity.
  • Growth: Join a rocket ship, learn every day, and accelerate your career in a collaborative, high-energy environment.
  • Fun: We take our work seriously, but not ourselves. Expect GIFs, puns, and the occasional ABM meme.

Base Salary Range: $188,997.50 - $255,863.00. The base salary range represents the anticipated low and high end of the base salary range for this position. We are seeking a highly organized, proactive, and detail-oriented Non-Technical Security Systems Program Manager to support our Client's Security Technology team by improving operational efficiency, driving consistency, and ensuring strategic initiatives and business-as-usual activities stay on track. The ideal candidate enjoys creating structure, developing processes, coordinating cross-functional projects, and transforming information into clear documentation, dashboards, and executive reporting. A strong understanding of how Security Systems organizations function within large global enterprises is important for success in this role. This is a full-time, fully remote position offering a comprehensive benefits package. Travel of approximately 15% will be required.

Responsibilities

  • Manage multiple projects and initiatives by developing project plans, timelines, milestones, and tracking deliverables.

  • Develop and maintain documentation that clearly defines roles, responsibilities, and workflows for internal teams, external partners, and vendors to ensure alignment and successful project execution.

  • Coordinate program intake and service onboarding activities, working with subject matter experts and cross-functional teams to develop and implement new processes and playbooks.

  • Facilitate ongoing collaboration and dialogue with key stakeholders for progress against the technology roadmap and project plans.

  • Identify opportunities to improve processes, increase efficiency, and standardize workflows across teams.

  • Maintain accurate project and program documentation and provide general operational support as needed to advance department and organizational objectives.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree required.

  • 5+ years of experience supporting Security Systems, Corporate Security, Physical Security, Facilities, or Technology teams within a large, global enterprise environment.

  • Experience developing dashboards, KPIs, executive reporting, SOPs, process documentation, reports, and executive presentations.

  • Exceptional organizational, communication, and time management skills.

  • Familiarity with Google Suite tools, technology, and applications.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while working independently and collaboratively.

Compensation

jobs.jobDescription:
The Payment Integrity team is a group of innovative thinkers sitting at the intersection of Clover's provider Network, Claims, and Tech teams. The Payment Integrity team ensures that Clover pays claims in an accurate manner, with a particular focus on reducing inappropriate medical spend.

As an DRG Inpatient Coding Validator at Clover Health, you will play a key role ensuring that Clover is able to continue to build and scale a compliant, efficient and profitable program. You will work to ensure quality assurance standards and regulatory policy are reflected in claims processing practices. You will help drive value for every member by ensuring that Clover’s medical claims are paid accurately and recovering overpayments when they are identified. The Associate - Inpatient Coder coordinates the identification of provider DRG denials and upcoding.

As an DRG Inpatient Coding Validator, you will:

  • Partner with Clinical, Claims, and Payment Integrity peers to review claims for DRG related issues on a prospective and retrospective basis that drive inaccurate payments to providers.
  • Proactively identify overpayments to ensure accurate claims payments on inpatient services.
  • Participate in collaborative discussions with MDs to verify the clinical rationale behind billed procedures.
  • Communicate effectively while building trust and lasting partnerships both laterally and vertically across multi-discipline teams.
  • Communicate effectively both internally and externally to ensure accurate claims adjudication and proper provider notification.

Success in this role looks like:

  • By the end of your initial 90-day period, you will have demonstrated a strong understanding of clinical coding practices and medical records review, while assisting our team in areas of DRG validation.
  • By 6 months, you will be working autonomously to execute within our clinical review workflows and will have developed strong interpersonal relationships across the organization.
  • Continued success in this position anchors in on developing a deep understanding of the workflows that support our clinical review life cycle, while maintaining regulatory compliance standards.

You should get in touch if:

  • You hold a CCS or CIC certification; required.
  • Knowledge of DRG pricing methodology; required.
  • You have at least 1 year of direct inpatient clinical coding experience.
  • Medicare or Medicare Advantage payment integrity or claims operations experience; preferred
  • You are technologically savvy with strong computer skills in Excel and PowerPoint.

Benefits Overview:

  • Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
  • Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.
  • Mental Well-Being: We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location.
  • Professional Development: Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks:

  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities
  • Reimbursement for office setup expenses
  • Monthly cell phone & internet stipend
  • Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams
  • Paid parental leave for all new parents
  • And much more!

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.

From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employee’s points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

Affect is transforming addiction treatment through an innovative, evidence-based digital program. We specialize in treating substance use disorders, such as opioid use disorder, stimulant use disorders, alcohol use disorder, and cannabis use disorder and we have expanded our services to include high-quality, accessible mental health. By combining mobile technology, counseling, and coordinated medical care, we empower our Members to reclaim their lives in recovery.

  • Conduct intake assessments to evaluate Member readiness and determine appropriate level of care
  • Facilitate group and one-on-one counseling sessions using Affect’s evidence-based curriculum
  • Provide crisis support and coordinate appropriate referrals when needed

  • Proficient with Microsoft Office or Google Suite, EMR systems, and telehealth platforms

  • The salary range for this full-time position is $55,000 - $70,000 and will commensurate with experience and professional license.

  • Supportive team culture focused on impact, collaboration, and innovation
  • Be part of building a modern, inclusive, and accessible addiction care system

Be part of the mission. Help us reshape the future of substance use disorder care!

The Role

As a Manager, Customer Success, you will lead a team of approximately 7-8 Customer Success Managers responsible for a combined portfolio of Upmarket customers with annual contract values ranging from $100K to $500K and representing approximately $15M-$20M in ARR.

You will be responsible for driving customer retention, adoption, customer value realization, and operational excellence across your team's portfolio while developing and coaching a high-performing team of Customer Success Managers. This role requires a strong people leader who can balance business performance, talent development, forecasting discipline, and customer outcomes.

Success in this role requires the ability to develop top talent, create accountability, establish operational rigor, and partner cross-functionally to ensure customers realize measurable business value from their investment in 6sense.

You will work closely with Sales, Professional Services, Support, Product, Marketing, and Revenue Operations to help customers achieve their goals while contributing to the continued growth and scale of the Customer Success organization.

What You'll Do

Lead and Develop a High-Performing Team

  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of approximately 7-8 Customer Success Managers supporting Upmarket customers.
  • Create a culture of accountability, customer-centricity, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Conduct regular coaching sessions, performance reviews, talent assessments, and career development conversations.
  • Establish clear expectations and operating rhythms that drive consistent execution and customer outcomes.
  • Recruit, onboard, and develop Customer Success talent while supporting succession planning across the organization.
  • Inspire and motivate a team that consistently delivers exceptional customer experiences and business results.

Drive Customer Success Outcomes

  • Lead a team responsible for customers with annual contract values between $100K and $500K and a combined portfolio of approximately $15M-$20M in ARR.
  • Drive strong Gross Revenue Retention (GRR), customer adoption, customer satisfaction, and value realization across the portfolio.
  • Coach Customer Success Managers on account strategy, executive stakeholder engagement, success planning, renewal strategy, risk mitigation, and value delivery, ensuring they understand and own the renewal process.
  • Ensure Customer Success Managers proactively identify customer risks and execute strategies to improve retention outcomes.
  • Partner with Sales leadership to align on customer health, growth opportunities, and strategic account planning.
  • Drive a high level of customer engagement and executive alignment across key accounts.

Drive Operational Excellence

  • Own portfolio forecasting processes, renewal inspections, customer health reviews, and risk management practices.
  • Ensure consistent execution of success plans, Executive Business Reviews (EBRs), account reviews, and customer engagement standards.
  • Use data and analytics to identify trends, improve performance, and drive informed decision-making.
  • Drive adoption of Customer Success processes, tools, and best practices across the team.
  • Champion initiatives that improve efficiency, scalability, forecast accuracy, and customer outcomes.

Partner Across the Business

  • Collaborate closely with Sales, Product, Professional Services, Support, Marketing, and RevOps to deliver a world-class customer experience.
  • Act as a voice of the customer and advocate for customer needs across the organization.
  • Support strategic initiatives focused on customer retention, product adoption, operational scale, and customer value realization.
  • Help shape the future of Customer Success programs, processes, and operating models as the business continues to grow.

  • 5+ years of people leadership experience leading customer-facing teams within a SaaS organization.
  • 8+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, Professional Services, Consulting, or other customer-facing roles.
  • Proven track record of building, developing, and retaining high-performing teams.
  • Experience leading teams responsible for customer retention, adoption, and customer outcomes.
  • Strong understanding of SaaS business models and key metrics, including GRR, churn, forecasting, customer health, and product adoption.
  • Experience coaching teams on executive engagement, account strategy, value realization, and risk management.
  • Excellent communication, coaching, and leadership skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive operational rigor and accountability through data-driven management practices.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate data into action.
  • Comfortable leveraging AI-powered tools and workflows to improve team productivity, customer insights, coaching effectiveness, and operational scale.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
  • Ability to travel up to 25% for customer meetings, team events, and company programs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading Customer Success teams supporting enterprise or upmarket SaaS customers.
  • Experience managing teams responsible for portfolios between $15M and $20M in ARR.
  • Experience within MarTech, AdTech, SalesTech, Revenue Technology, or related B2B SaaS industries.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce, Gainsight, Clari, Gong, and other customer success technologies.
  • Experience helping scale Customer Success organizations, teams, and operating models.

At 6sense, you'll have the opportunity to lead a talented team, influence the future of Customer Success, and directly impact customer retention and business outcomes across a diverse portfolio of Upmarket customers.

You'll work alongside some of the industry's most innovative leaders while helping customers transform how they identify, engage, and convert buyers. You'll have the autonomy to make an impact, the support of a world-class leadership team, and the opportunity to grow your career while developing the next generation of Customer Success talent.

If you're passionate about building great teams, creating exceptional customer outcomes, and helping scale a world-class Customer Success organization, we'd love to hear from you.
